frequency_question: How often do major debt management buyback or liquidity programs scale up to their maximum planned operational volumes within 28 months of launch?
membership_rule: Includes formalized, ongoing structural Treasury or central bank bond buyback/liquidity operations intended for debt management or market functioning; excludes emergency one-off bailouts or purely monetary policy rate-setting operations.

cases.name: Federal Reserve Large-Scale Asset Purchases (QE1-QE3 scaling)
Bank of England Gilt Purchase and Sale Operations expansion
ECB Public Sector Purchase Programme (PSPP) volume ramp-up
Bank of Japan Yield Curve Control operational volume adjustments

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named; represents the complete set of major structural sovereign bond purchase program scale-ups by G4 central banks/treasuries in the modern fiat era.
known_gaps: None of these are strictly US Treasury debt management buybacks for liquidity, but rather central bank QE/YCC programs, though the structural scaling dynamics under market pressure are highly analogous.
skeleton: Four major structural sovereign debt intervention programs across G4 jurisdictions over the past 18 years, all of which successfully scaled past initial conservative pilot volumes to meet or exceed target operational capacities.
validity_reason: Structural mechanics of central bank and treasury liquidity interventions change slowly across institutional frameworks.
